sections.content: How many people are "public services associate professionals"?

42,590 people

were counted on the census as "public services associate professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Public services associate professionals supervise, manage and undertake general administrative work in national and local government departments, organise the activities of local offices of national government departments, and promote the image and understanding of an organisation and its products and services to consumers and other specified audiences.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "public services associate professionals", 14.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "public services associate professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "public services associate professionals" included:

  • credit controllers
  • housing officers
  • other vocational and industrial trainers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "public services associate professionals" there were more women than men (67% compared with 33%).

This means "public services associate professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 33% and women made up 67% of "public services associate professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "public services associate professionals" included:

  • teachers of english as a foreign language
  • teaching professionals (other)
  • legal associate professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "public services associate professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "public services associate professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "public services associate professionals", 13.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75.4% compared with 24.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98%) than self-employed (2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
